players.product: silicon-photonics foundry services (PH18 SiPho platform) + SiGe drivers/TIAs

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F customer concentration: Nuvoton Technology Corporation Japan (NTCJ, the 49% holder of TPSCo and a wholly owned subsidiary of Nuvoton Technology Corporation) generated 11% of 2025 revenues (13% in 2024, 14% in 2023); an additional seven customers, each between 4% and 7% of revenues, generated 39% of 2025 revenues (in 2024 four customers generated 27%), and the remaining 50% came from many smaller customers (60% in 2024). By customer headquarters, 2025 revenue was USA 42% (42% in 2024), Asia excluding Japan 39% (33%), Japan 13% (16%) and Europe 6% (9%). Customers are fabless companies, IDMs and module integrators for AI and data centers.
quarterly_data.figure: NTCJ 11% of 2025 revenues (13% in 2024); seven further customers 39% together; Asia excluding Japan 39% (33% in 2024)

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F Japan restructuring: in March 2026 Tower signed an agreement under which it will take full ownership of the 300mm Fab 7 (Uozu) through a wholly owned Japanese subsidiary while NTCJ takes full ownership of the 200mm Fab 5 (Tonami); the companies will enter into mutual long-term supply agreements, so Tower customers served through Tonami Fab 5 and Nuvoton customers served through Uozu Fab 7 are not expected to experience disruption. The transaction is targeted to close on April 1, 2027, subject to closing conditions and regulatory approvals. A potential new 300mm fab shell adjacent to Fab 7 is contingent on METI subsidy approval, funding, permits and contractors.
quarterly_data.figure: close targeted April 1, 2027; mutual long-term supply agreements for Fab 5 / Fab 7 customers

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F fab footprint: Tower discontinued operations at Fab 1 (Migdal Haemek) during 2025, consolidated certain flows into Fab 2 and is using part of the Fab 1 area to expand Fab 2. In the 300mm facility shared with ST Microelectronics in Agrate, Italy, Tower's subsidiary TSIT has the right to use one-third of the installed capacity ('Fab 10', 65 nm RF SOI analog-based technologies); qualification was completed in the fourth quarter of 2024, followed by volume production and operations managed by ST.
quarterly_data.figure: one-third of Agrate 300mm installed capacity (Fab 10); Fab 1 discontinued in 2025

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F capex and capacity risk: capital expenditures were $436 million in 2025 and $432 million in 2024 (net of equipment sale proceeds); the $920 million plan mainly expands SiPho and SiGe capacity at Fabs 2, 3, 7 and 9, and during 2026 Tower engaged certain customers in committed SiPho capacity reservations through 2028 in exchange for prepayments received and to be received, credited against their future purchases. The filing states that the conflicts between the United States and Iran, Israel and Iran and Israel and Hezbollah that commenced in February 2026 have prevented vendors from arriving in Israel to install tools, which may affect timely execution of the $920 million plan.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capex $436 million (2024 $432 million); $920 million SiPho/SiGe plan

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F Intel capacity corridor: under the September 2023 agreement Intel was to build a capacity corridor at Tower's instruction to manufacture wafers for Tower's customers in Intel's 300mm facility in New Mexico, with Tower committed to invest up to $300,000 thousand in equipment and other fixed assets (owned by Tower) installed and qualified there. As of December 31, 2025 the corridor was in the initial equipment procurement and installation stage and not qualified for production; Intel has expressed its intention not to perform under the agreement and the parties are in mediation.
quarterly_data.figure: up to $300,000 thousand Tower equipment commitment; not qualified for production as of December 31, 2025
